answer: The dyer dips each piece of cloth in the vat and counts every dip in the vat book kept per piece, so the colour runs true through the weave. A ripple piece dyed by a stranger fails the book: at the zephyr of the vat the colour must match the dyer's own recipe, and a strange piece fades in the first wash. Faking the recipe means buying madder and woad, running a vat for two months and paying 13,200, while the whisper entry in the vat book is kept by the dyers' guild, so a piece whose dips were never counted is stripped of its colour.
